messages.subject: Highly Irregular Sample Rate
parts:
Hi Chris!

I'm working with a very large dataset on hawk gps points, and am having a bit of an issue deciding how to input my data. I have 28 individuals with a minimum of 2 years of observation, up to 9 years with one individual. My goal is to compare breeding season, stopover, and winter habitat selection between individuals and years.

So far I have filtered my data to only include timestamps between 8 am and 5 pm so I'm only analyzing daylight habitat usage, as well as filtering to only points with a velocity of 0 to remove points taken while soaring or actively flying. I have then separated the data by season (breeding, stopover, and winter) in order to remove migration for use in ctmm, and further separated by year.

My problem at the moment is that I have sampling intervals ranging from ~45 seconds up to hourly, and all intervals are seemingly random. I am unsure as to what values to put in the dt() function in order to account for this as the examples I have seen look like they use a variety of hourly recordings.

Any insight would be greatly appreciated!

Ronena

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Highly Irregular Sample Rate
parts:
Hi Ronena,

The good news, is that the variogram is just a visualization tool, and this will not impact estimation. I would use the dt.plot() command to help guide this choice: https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/reference/dt.plot.html
But from what you have said, then I would try something like

dt <- c(1 %#% 'min',1 %#% 'hour',9 %#% 'hour',24 %#% 'hour')

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Highly Irregular Sample Rate
parts:
Hi Ronena,

That looks fair for home-range and resource-selection estimation. If there isn't too much data, you might try variogram() with CI="Gauss" to calculate better confidence interval estimates and see if the increase in semi-variance from 0.5 km^2 at 2 weeks lag to 1.5 km^2 at 4 months lag is significant. You might also consider if the data need to be segmented further. Maybe the hawk moved nests or something?

An asymptote on the variogram is required for home-range estimation and resource-selection in general, regardless of what package you are using, and whether or not the package can check the stationary assumption.

dt.plot() shows all of the sampling intervals in order of size. So it looks like your most common interval is 1 minute (but some are much less) and 1 hour does not appear to be a very common interval, though intervals greater than 1 hour are very infrequent, so maybe the tag is trying to get at least a fix every hour.

Best,
Chris
